title: The Panassie film made in France and Biarritz
summary: They discuss the jazz film by Hugues Panassie's son, with Jones and Buckner on screen, and Jones's unplanned drum solo at Biarritz.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: I remember that year before last, I think it was, Hugues Panassie's son, Hugues Panassio the great jazz impresario who lives in France and has contributed a great

deal to jazz - his son came over here and did a movie. It was like a discography of jazz. He got you, he got Buck Clayton. I did some with him. He did some with you in Europe. Then he came over here and did something with Jimmy Crawford.
That's right, 'jazz and all that,' which is a movie that's all the way in Europe.
I saw some of the movies he did of you and Milt Buckner in France and they were just amazing and I haven't seen anything like that here in the United States.

What Louis Panassie in France to do with this thing - he would like to come over to take it out to the colleges himself. He don't want to give it to nobody else because he wants it to be for educational purposes. He's going to do that. Other people would love to get it. I mean the networks such as CBS, NBC - they'd love to get it but he will not give it to them because he don't want it like that, because he's trying to do something in regards to his father, Hugues Panassie. I just got through doing the thing with Jimmy Slide and he did a whole thing that's in the movie that Mr. Duke Ellington's whole entire band is on the thing. This thing is going to be coming out to go around to all the colleges of the United States. It's an educational thing. Right now it is in Europe; it is in France, in Spain, in Germany and what have you.
I saw one of the most wonderful things of you, about 15 minutes of drum solos by you, in some little small club over there and it was just absolutely beautiful.
Oh, this was horrible. It was in -
It was horrible? I thought it was beautiful.
Yes, because I didn't know it was a movie. I was going out to play tennis and I went down and I had on a shirt -
Do you still play tennis, Jo?
Yes. So I went down and I said, 'What are you doing?' They got the cameras and all this. We were in Biarritz. That's right on the border of the south of France, before you go into Spain.
What are you doing now, right now? This is 1973 and in the next 3 or 4 days I think you were getting ready to go back.
I had planned to join Milt Buckner in Europe.
Have you got any particular place to start?
